title: Trump Presents Irish Open Trophy to Shane Lowry, Pledges to 'Take the Tariffs Off' Irish Whiskey
detail: President Trump, wrapping up his two-day Ireland visit on Sunday, September 13, 2026, delayed his scheduled morning departure to watch the Irish Open's final round at his Doonbeg golf course, where home favorite Shane Lowry closed with a 63 for an 11-shot, tournament-record victory. Trump watched the winning putt from his VIP suite with sons Eric and Don Jr., then joined Taoiseach Micheál Martin in presenting Lowry the trophy. Asked about Irish whiskey during the ceremony, Trump said 'I am going to take the tariffs off' on behalf of the United States, citing requests from the Taoiseach and others present. Speaking to reporters earlier at Doonbeg, Trump also addressed the Russia-Ukraine war and high US gas prices, saying 'this isn't done by the Middle East. This is done by what's happening with Russia and Ukraine,' and urging President Zelenskyy to 'stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia' because it was 'hurting... the world.' On Iran, Trump said Tehran 'wants to make a deal so badly. They are calling constantly,' but added 'they got to make the right deal. I'm not going to make a deal that's no good,' while again predicting the six-month war would end 'right after the midterms, maybe before.' His comments came a day ahead of a planned Monday meeting in Oman between Iran, Iraq and Gulf Cooperation Council states on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which Trump said was 'up to them' and which the US is not party to. Also at Doonbeg, Trump raised the possibility of an open-ended US troop presence in Iran, telling reporters 'we'll ultimately get out, unless we decide to stay and keep the oil, like Venezuela,' a reference to the US military's continued presence guarding Syrian and Venezuelan-adjacent oil infrastructure in past conflicts.

media.caption: Trump prepares to present the Irish Open trophy to Shane Lowry at his Doonbeg golf course

title: Trump Dismisses AI CEOs' Bipartisan Call to Slow Development, Says 'Whoever Wins AI, Wins'
detail: President Trump, speaking to reporters Sunday, September 13, 2026, rejected a rare joint call from the CEOs of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI urging the industry and government to slow the pace of frontier AI development over safety concerns, arguing the US cannot afford to cede ground to China. 'We're leading China in AI, we're the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins,' Trump said, dismissing warnings about the technology's risks as exaggerated and claiming 'negative forces' were behind the alarm. He singled out Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei for criticism over Amodei's public warnings that AI development was outpacing safety guardrails. House Speaker Mike Johnson separately downplayed calls for federal AI regulation. In a Truth Social post, Trump blamed a 'SICK conspiracy' for growing public backlash against AI data center construction in local communities, saying 'the only one that is happy about it is China.'

media.caption: Trump dismissed calls from AI industry leaders to slow development, saying the US cannot fall behind China
